title: Linux.Bew_Backdoor_Investigation_e01
description: Investigate and respond to a potential security incident involving the Linux.Bew backdoor malware.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The target system has exhibited unusual network activity, including unexpected outbound connections to an unknown server. Initial analysis suggests the presence of a backdoor malware known as Linux.Bew, which is used for Bitcoin mining and data exfiltration. Your task is to investigate and respond to this potential security incident.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have SSH access to the target system with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. The target system's IP address is `192.168.50.5`. Enter the word `start` to proceed to the next level.
levels.local_content: Local sandbox access is not required for this scenario. Enter the word `start` to proceed to the next level.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content: Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service running on the target system. Enumerate running services and distinguish legitimate from suspicious services.
levels.solution: Check the systemd services and look for any unusual or unauthorized services. The service name `bkd.service` should be identified as suspicious. The flag type is a service name.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the systemd services and look for any unusual or unauthorized services. Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all services.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services that are not part of the standard system or applications you have installed. The suspicious service might have an unusual name or description.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot. Identify persistence mechanisms (e.g., systemd, cron, scheduled task).
levels.solution: Examine the systemd service configuration files for any suspicious entries. The persistence mechanism should be identified as the systemd service `bkd.service`. The flag type is a service name.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Examine the systemd service configuration files for any suspicious entries. Use the command `systemctl cat bkd.service` to view the service configuration.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for any unusual paths or commands in the service configuration that might indicate malicious activity.

levels.title: Locate Suspicious File
levels.content: Locate the executable or file associated with the suspicious activity. Correlate processes with files on disk and identify malicious artifacts.
levels.solution: Investigate the service configuration to find the path of the executable. The filename `/usr/local/bin/lab-checkin.sh` should be identified as the suspicious file. The flag type is a file path.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Investigate the service configuration to find the path of the executable. Use the command `ps aux | grep bkd` to find the process associated with the service.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for any unusual file paths or commands in the process list that might indicate malicious activity.
